reconcile.connective: Gill collapses the two rubrics into one: the "good" that earns the resurrection of life just is believing in Christ.

discrepancy.connective: Rudolf Bultmann judged John 5:28-29's deeds-based verdict a later redactor's addition, clashing with the Gospel's own faith-based, already-realized judgment.

skeptic.name: Rudolf Bultmann
skeptic.work: The Gospel of John: A Commentary
skeptic.attribution: Rudolf Bultmann (d. 1976), The Gospel of John: A Commentary (German 1941; Eng. trans. 1971)

excerpts.excerpt_text: they that have done good; which none of Adam's posterity naturally do, or can do of themselves: such are designed here who believe in Christ, which to do is the work of God, and the greatest and best of worlds; and without which it is impossible to please God in any; and indeed, whatever is not of faith is sin, and cannot be a good work: a good work is that which is done according to the will of God, from love to him, in faith, and with a view to his glory …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill glosses 'they that have done good' (the works-criterion of John 5:29's resurrection judgment) as meaning those who believe in Christ, explicitly folding the works-rubric into the faith-rubric that is central to this contradiction.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible, on John 5:29 (1746-63)
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill's own exposition of John 5:29 treats this exact passage, reducing 'done good' to believing in Christ; Haley's doctrinal 'Justification: By Faith / By Works' chapter covers only the separate Paul-vs-James dispute (Rom. 3-4, Gal. 2-3 vs. James 2) and does not engage this Gospel verse set, so the surfaced commentator is used instead.
